method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and EURACAN, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.102977) 'Merkel-cell carcinoma: ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up' (published 30 April 2024), 18 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at NCBI PMC efetch JATS <license> element for PMC11145756 (Europe PMC returned HTTP 503 on 2026-09-23)). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (treatment protocols, not guidelines) 'eviQ protocols 3463 Merkel cell carcinoma metastatic avelumab (v.10) and 1023 Skin cancer Merkel cell carcinoma adjuvant EBRT post-operative (v.5)' (current versions retrieved 24 September 2026), 9 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (eviQ 'Disclaimer and copyright' page). eviQ also states that its content should not be hosted on external sites, and that commercial entities must contact eviQ to seek permission (https://www.eviq.org.au/copyright). Adaptations must cite the eviQ ID, version and URL. (read at https://www.eviq.org.au/copyright (Disclaimer and copyright page)). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 keeps every ESMO-EURACAN claim (S1) unchanged and adds S2, two Australian eviQ treatment protocols (CC BY-NC 4.0, paraphrased): avelumab for metastatic disease (https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3463) and post-operative radiotherapy (https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1023), for the avelumab dose, premedication and monitoring, and Australian radiotherapy indications and dose prescriptions, which S1 does not give. The S2 source file concatenates the two protocol pages, each under a header line naming its URL; only protocol text from the ID line to the literature-search section was kept. The radiotherapy dose-prescription tables survived conversion as text and are anchored where used. No Australian Merkel cell carcinoma guideline was found (the Cancer Council keratinocyte guideline does not cover it).

claims.claim: **Australia has the world's highest incidence** (Queensland age-adjusted rate 1.6 per 100000). Here about 80% of cases are UV-driven and 20% polyomavirus-driven, the reverse of Europe and North America.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and EURACAN, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.102977), 'Merkel-cell carcinoma: ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up', published 30 April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11145756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Risk factors:** older age (median 76), male sex, pale skin, UV exposure and immunosuppression, which accounts for about 10% of patients (transplant recipients, haematological cancer, HIV).
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and EURACAN, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.102977), 'Merkel-cell carcinoma: ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up', published 30 April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11145756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Typical lesion:** a fast-growing, painless, firm pink to violet dome or plaque of 1–2 cm on sun-exposed skin, most often head and neck. It is easily mistaken for BCC, SCC, amelanotic melanoma or benign lesions; dermatoscopy helps.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and EURACAN, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.102977), 'Merkel-cell carcinoma: ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up', published 30 April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11145756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine the regional lymph nodes and assess comorbidity and life expectancy;** confirm the diagnosis histologically with H&E and the dedicated immunostain panel.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and EURACAN, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.102977), 'Merkel-cell carcinoma: ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up', published 30 April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11145756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Imaging is mandatory:** CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis (plus head and neck for primaries there), with whole-body FDG-PET/CT preferred where available.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and EURACAN, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.102977), 'Merkel-cell carcinoma: ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up', published 30 April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11145756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do sentinel node biopsy with the primary excision** to detect occult nodal disease; it is less reliable in the immunosuppressed and in head, neck or midline-trunk tumours.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and EURACAN, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.102977), 'Merkel-cell carcinoma: ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up', published 30 April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11145756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Every decision belongs to a multidisciplinary team with real Merkel cell experience,** ideally with trial access.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and EURACAN, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.102977), 'Merkel-cell carcinoma: ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up', published 30 April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11145756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Wide local excision with 1–2 cm margins;** if that is not achievable, 0.5–1.0 cm margins plus adjuvant radiotherapy may do. Definitive radiotherapy is the alternative when excision is not feasible.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and EURACAN, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.102977), 'Merkel-cell carcinoma: ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up', published 30 April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11145756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Adjuvant radiotherapy of 50–60 Gy to the tumour bed** for tumours 1 cm or larger or with adverse features (stage IB or higher). Observation alone in stage IA is a referral-centre decision.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and EURACAN, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.102977), 'Merkel-cell carcinoma: ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up', published 30 April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11145756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Positive sentinel node:** adjuvant nodal radiotherapy, with or without completion dissection, after MDT review. Clinically involved nodes or extranodal spread: node dissection plus postoperative radiotherapy (or definitive radiotherapy if inoperable).
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and EURACAN, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.102977), 'Merkel-cell carcinoma: ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up', published 30 April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11145756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not give adjuvant chemotherapy;** offer trials of (neo)adjuvant immunotherapy instead.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and EURACAN, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.102977), 'Merkel-cell carcinoma: ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up', published 30 April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11145756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Australian adjuvant radiotherapy protocol (eviQ):** for T1–4, any N, M0 disease with no gross tumour left after surgery, ECOG 0–2. After MDT discussion radiotherapy can be left out when every favourable feature is present: margins of 1 cm or more, a primary of 1 cm or less, a negative sentinel node, no chronic immunosuppression, no lymphovascular invasion and a primary outside the head and neck. Treat the primary site alone if the sentinel node is negative and imaging shows no suspicious nodes.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (treatment protocols, not guidelines), 'eviQ protocols 3463 Merkel cell carcinoma metastatic avelumab (v.10) and 1023 Skin cancer Merkel cell carcinoma adjuvant EBRT post-operative (v.5)', current versions retrieved 24 September 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3463, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Start radiotherapy once the wound has healed, ideally 4–6 weeks after surgery;** wait for a skin graft to take fully. PET staging before surgery, where available, helps with work-up and follow-up. With positive margins the MDT weighs further surgery against delaying radiotherapy, since a boost may make re-excision unnecessary.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (treatment protocols, not guidelines), 'eviQ protocols 3463 Merkel cell carcinoma metastatic avelumab (v.10) and 1023 Skin cancer Merkel cell carcinoma adjuvant EBRT post-operative (v.5)', current versions retrieved 24 September 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3463, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Adjuvant radiotherapy doses (eviQ, 2 Gy fractions to the high-risk volume):** clear margins (R0) 50–54 Gy in 25–27 fractions; microscopically positive margins or extracapsular extension (R1) 60 Gy recommended, with 54 Gy an option for small T1 tumours; gross residual disease (R2) 60–66 Gy. Hypofractionated options for the primary are 45–50 Gy in 20 fractions over 4 weeks, or 30 Gy in 6 fractions over 3 weeks.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (treatment protocols, not guidelines), 'eviQ protocols 3463 Merkel cell carcinoma metastatic avelumab (v.10) and 1023 Skin cancer Merkel cell carcinoma adjuvant EBRT post-operative (v.5)', current versions retrieved 24 September 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3463, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **First line for inoperable or disseminated disease is a PD-1 or PD-L1 antibody** rather than chemotherapy, being more effective and safer. Avelumab, pembrolizumab, retifanlimab and nivolumab are all recommended in the first or second line unless contraindicated.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and EURACAN, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.102977), 'Merkel-cell carcinoma: ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up', published 30 April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11145756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Avelumab (JAVELIN Merkel trial):** in untreated patients the response rate was 39.7% with median survival 20.3 months; outcomes are best when it is used first line, and immunosuppressed patients benefit too.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and EURACAN, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.102977), 'Merkel-cell carcinoma: ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up', published 30 April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11145756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No biomarker predicts benefit** (PD-L1, viral status, tumour mutational burden and CD8 infiltration all failed), and the best duration of immunotherapy is unknown.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and EURACAN, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.102977), 'Merkel-cell carcinoma: ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up', published 30 April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11145756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oligometastatic progression:** consider surgery or stereotactic radiotherapy in fit patients, but start with systemic immunotherapy. If immunotherapy is contraindicated or fails, palliative radiotherapy or chemotherapy are options of uncertain survival benefit.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and EURACAN, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.102977), 'Merkel-cell carcinoma: ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up', published 30 April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11145756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avelumab 10 mg/kg IV on day 1 every 14 days, or 800 mg every 14 days (no more than 10 mg/kg below 80 kg), until progression or unacceptable toxicity,** for unresectable or metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma. It is a PBS authority item, and doses are never reduced.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (treatment protocols, not guidelines), 'eviQ protocols 3463 Merkel cell carcinoma metastatic avelumab (v.10) and 1023 Skin cancer Merkel cell carcinoma adjuvant EBRT post-operative (v.5)', current versions retrieved 24 September 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3463, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Infusion reactions are a high risk with avelumab, some severe:** give paracetamol 1,000 mg and loratadine 10 mg by mouth 60 minutes before each of the first four infusions, and keep premedicating after any mild or moderate reaction.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (treatment protocols, not guidelines), 'eviQ protocols 3463 Merkel cell carcinoma metastatic avelumab (v.10) and 1023 Skin cancer Merkel cell carcinoma adjuvant EBRT post-operative (v.5)', current versions retrieved 24 September 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3463, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Seek expert advice first** if the patient has significant autoimmune disease, an organ transplant, past viral hepatitis or previous lung radiotherapy. Radiation recall has been seen with PD-L1 inhibitors, so time the start carefully after a long course of radiotherapy.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (treatment protocols, not guidelines), 'eviQ protocols 3463 Merkel cell carcinoma metastatic avelumab (v.10) and 1023 Skin cancer Merkel cell carcinoma adjuvant EBRT post-operative (v.5)', current versions retrieved 24 September 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3463, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Early apparent growth can be pseudoprogression (about 5%):** if the patient is well, consider continuing and rescanning 4 to 6 weeks later.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (treatment protocols, not guidelines), 'eviQ protocols 3463 Merkel cell carcinoma metastatic avelumab (v.10) and 1023 Skin cancer Merkel cell carcinoma adjuvant EBRT post-operative (v.5)', current versions retrieved 24 September 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3463, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Tests:** FBC, EUC, eGFR, liver tests, cortisol, thyroid function and glucose at baseline; FBC, EUC, eGFR, liver tests and glucose before every cycle; thyroid function (and consider cortisol) every 4–6 weeks on treatment and 12-weekly afterwards. Screen for hepatitis before starting.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (treatment protocols, not guidelines), 'eviQ protocols 3463 Merkel cell carcinoma metastatic avelumab (v.10) and 1023 Skin cancer Merkel cell carcinoma adjuvant EBRT post-operative (v.5)', current versions retrieved 24 September 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3463, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **eviQ calls the evidence limited, resting mainly on the phase II JAVELIN Merkel 200 trial.** After chemotherapy (part A, 88 patients), 33.0% responded (10 completely), responses lasted a median of 40.5 months, and median PFS and survival were 2.7 and 12.6 months. Grade 3 treatment-related events were 5% in part A and 20.5% in untreated patients (part B), where 23.1% had infusion reactions and 15.4% stopped for toxicity.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (treatment protocols, not guidelines), 'eviQ protocols 3463 Merkel cell carcinoma metastatic avelumab (v.10) and 1023 Skin cancer Merkel cell carcinoma adjuvant EBRT post-operative (v.5)', current versions retrieved 24 September 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3463, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Use geriatric and comorbidity assessment to guide treatment;** radiotherapy alone suits those unfit for surgery, and checkpoint inhibitors are the preferred systemic therapy in older patients with inoperable disease.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and EURACAN, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.102977), 'Merkel-cell carcinoma: ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up', published 30 April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11145756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Relapse risk peaks in the first 2–3 years.** Review every 3–6 months for 3 years, 6-monthly to year 5, then yearly for life with a full skin check; cross-sectional imaging may be offered to higher-risk patients.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and EURACAN, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.102977), 'Merkel-cell carcinoma: ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up', published 30 April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11145756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Teach whole-skin self-examination:** these patients are at higher risk of further skin cancers. MCPyV oncoprotein antibody tracking is of uncertain value but may be used if seropositive at baseline.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and EURACAN, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.102977), 'Merkel-cell carcinoma: ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up', published 30 April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11145756/, retrieved 2026-09-23
